title: The Power of Habit, lesson 1 - your life runs on autopilot

slides.title: Why You Do Things You Never _Decided_ To Do
Take This 10-Second Test

graphic.title: Before 9am today, did you...
graphic.note: Tick every one you did. Then ask: how many did you actually decide to do?

body: Most mornings feel like a series of choices.
But how many of these did you **actually decide** to do?
One man's strange story shows what's really going on.

slides.title: Meet The Man Who Couldn't Remember

graphic.note: If you couldn't form new memories, which of these could you still do? Guess, then swipe.

body: In 1992, a viral infection destroyed the parts of **Eugene Pauly's** brain that store new memories.
He couldn't hold onto a new fact for more than *a few moments.*

slides.title: He Couldn't Draw His House. He Never Got Lost.
body: Asked to sketch his new home, Eugene **couldn't.** Yet when hungry, he walked straight to the kitchen.
He walked his neighbourhood every day and always found his way home, _with no idea how._

slides.title: Then A Scientist Tested It

graphic.line2: He still picked the marked one, more often every week.

body: Researcher **Larry Squire** showed Eugene pairs of objects, one secretly marked as correct.
Over weeks, Eugene got better and better, with *no memory* of ever seeing them.

slides.title: Memory And Habit Run On Separate Tracks
body: Squire concluded that habits live in an older brain region, the _basal ganglia_, which Eugene's illness had spared.
So a habit can keep running **even when you have no idea why.**

slides.title: So How Much Of Your Day Is Autopilot?
body: Duhigg cites a 2006 Duke University study suggesting **more than 40%** of our daily actions are habits, not decisions.
Now picture that in *your* day.

slides.title: Try To Answer These Without Thinking

items: Which side of the bed do you leave?
What did you do first today?
graphic.note: Hard to answer? That's autopilot at work.

body: You do these every single day.
You're **doing** them. But you're not really **choosing** them.

slides.title: What You Notice Is Just The Tip
body: That's unsettling. But it's also **good news.**
If so much of life runs on autopilot, *noticing* the pattern is the first step to steering it.

slides.title: Try The One-Hour Watch Tomorrow
body: Pick one ordinary hour. Screenshot this. **Tally every automatic act.**
How many things happened *before* you decided to do them?

slides.title: One Question To Sit With

graphic.q: Which of your habits would keep running even if you forgot why you started them?

body: Most of your day isn't decided. **It's repeated.**
Save this, and follow for lesson 2. Full animated lesson at *visualgrowth.app*
